status: 100-round campaign authorized; preparing frozen oracle and cold-process baseline

objective.assumption: User explicitly selected cold process startup with an unchanged prompt and fixed randomness.
objective.score: Median end-to-end cold-process wall time, correctness as PASS/FAIL gate only.
objective.timer_start: Immediately before the evaluator launches a new native process.
objective.timer_end: Native process exits after completing video/audio encoding and closing its MP4.
included: all weight loading and model preparation
excluded_but_reported: post-run unit comparisons and media checks
objective.gpu_seconds: Sum of device reservation durations; for N GPUs held throughout a request, N times end-to-end seconds.
objective.selection: For the authorized 100-round campaign, use one H200 and select solely by confirmed cold-process E2E seconds after the fixed correctness PASS gate. GPU count/cost frontiers are future study options, not additional ranking objectives in this run.
objective.file_cache_policy: New process/model/CUDA state for every sample. Shared OS/filesystem caches are not forcibly cleared; this is not a guaranteed cold-storage benchmark.

mutable_surface.description: The whole candidate C/C++/CUDA implementation can change, including new kernels and runtime architecture. Numeric knob tuning is only a subset.
mutable_surface.native_runtime_requirement: Keep a native CUDA executable; Python may orchestrate experiments and evaluate outputs, but is not an inference runtime dependency.

files: official PyTorch source and its source pins
requirements: original checkpoint values and mixed-precision contract
all text/video/audio tokens and their positions
20 model evaluations and original sigma/Euler semantics
fixed VAE tile boundaries and overlap semantics
excluded_optimizations: request-dependent work before the timing boundary
frozen_surface.arithmetic_note: Implementation rewrites may change rounding only if all fixed numeric checks pass. Preserve existing BF16 rounding boundaries first; do not assume a small local error is safe over 20 steps.

evaluation.correctness_oracle: Pinned official Diffusers/PyTorch on CUDA; separate from the performance baseline.
evaluation.performance_baseline: Accepted native release 14274 is the one-H200 anchor. For N-GPU candidates, also compare against the best correct implementation at the same N/topology once available; do not imply the seed already supports N-GPU execution. Use exactly the same requests, timing mode and CPU resources.
screening_stages: Compile and ABI checks with a timeout.
Replay the fixed primitive inputs/outputs and captured real activation checks; do not recompute PyTorch reference operators per candidate.
Affected block or single-forward diagnostic against the frozen reference.
Full independent 20-step trajectories and float video/audio decoder checks, using each implementation's own evolving state.
Three isolated cold-process timing samples with the fixed prompt and seed; run the complete 6+1 correctness regression and five paired cold-process comparisons before keeping an improvement.
evaluation.fixture_policy: PyTorch oracle outputs are frozen once; each candidate is compared with fixed tensors. No large reference-model execution per trial. Fixed-reference-input velocities and independently evolving candidate trajectories are both checked.
evaluation.precision_limits: Read the existing contract without relaxation. Non-finite outputs, incomplete video/audio, missing stages or missing files fail.

measurement_protocol.initial_design: The active protocol uses three measured candidate samples. Every sample launches a fresh native process with the same prompt and seed 7; no warm or changed-prompt request contributes to ranking.
measurement_protocol.order: For promotion, alternate parent/candidate and candidate/parent order over five pairs on one exclusively reserved H200, using a fresh process for every sample.
measurement_protocol.promotion: Require the complete fixed 6+1 correctness gate. Median paired improvement must exceed max(0.5% of parent median, 2*MAD(paired differences)/sqrt(5)); at least four of five pairs must favor the candidate. This noise guard applies to the single latency score. The authoritative details are in runs/20261010-100/protocol.json.
measurement_protocol.profiling: Profiler runs diagnose CUDA API overhead, kernel time, copies and communication. Their wall times are excluded from the score.
measurement_protocol.concurrency: Agents may generate and compile candidates concurrently; timing workers use exclusive GPU sets. Baseline and candidate use the same CPU allocation and host thread limits.
measurement_protocol.reproducibility: Log source/build/harness/input hashes, hardware topology, library versions, environment, GPU clocks/temperature, and all raw results.

search_loop.selection: Profile the current end-to-end critical path; choose a bounded hypothesis from search_space.json or propose another semantics-preserving implementation.
search_loop.execution: Create an isolated candidate checkout/build, apply one interpretable change, compile, screen, validate, benchmark, then record keep/discard/crash with the reason.
search_loop.frontier: Retain about three diverse correct candidates per GPU class when justified; test combinations after their dependencies are satisfied.
search_loop.budgets: Use separate limits for compilation, correctness, profiling, timing and the whole campaign. The original autoresearch five-minute training window is not this task's score or a literal required duration.
search_loop.launch_status: User authorized 100 distinct candidate rounds; one H200 is fixed for this initial workflow trial.

first_experiments: E0: freeze the PyTorch unit oracle once and measure the accepted seed with fresh processes, the fixed prompt, and seed 7.
E1: optimize cold-process startup and preparation inside the timing boundary; score only complete fixed-prompt, fixed-seed MP4 generation.
E2: reuse MLP/attention scratch without changing arithmetic or GEMM shape.
E3: cache existing cuBLASLt/cuDNN descriptors and execution plans before changing algorithms.
E4: implement an FP32 GPU sampler and keep packed latents on device while preserving Euler rounding behavior.
E5: use profiles to choose audio-convolution optimization, video-VAE GPU stitching, or elementwise fusion.
Future study, outside the active one-H200 campaign: test two-GPU distribution of unchanged video VAE tiles and concurrent video/audio decoding.
Future study, outside the active one-H200 campaign: compare TP2 and Ulysses2 for DiT, then expand to 4/8 GPUs only when measurements justify it.
